All datasets used on this website, with what we learned about each one: how to access it, its resolution,
how often it is updated and its current status. All data belongs to its respective owners.

## Landsat WELD true-colour annual composite

- **Provider:** NASA GIBS (imagery: USGS/NASA Landsat)
- **Link:** <https://nasa-gibs.github.io/gibs-api-docs/>
- **Access:** Tile service (WMTS), no login
- **Spatial resolution:** 30 m (shown up to zoom 12)
- **Temporal coverage:** 2010 annual composite
- **Update frequency:** Static (historical product)
- **Status:** Active
- **License / citation:** NASA open data. Acknowledge NASA GIBS / ESDIS

## Harmonized Landsat Sentinel-2 (HLS) Landsat Surface Reflectance (HLSL30 v2.0)

- **Provider:** NASA GIBS (data: NASA LP DAAC, imagery: USGS/NASA Landsat 8 and 9)
- **Link:** <https://doi.org/10.5067/HLS/HLSL30.002>
- **Access:** Tile service (WMTS), no login. One layer per day
- **Spatial resolution:** 30 m (shown up to zoom 12)
- **Temporal coverage:** Nov 2020–present, daily (a few missing days)
- **Update frequency:** Daily, ~2–4 days delay
- **Status:** Active
- **License / citation:** NASA open data. Cite: Masek et al., HLS Operational Land Surface Reflectance V2.0, LP DAAC. Acknowledge NASA GIBS / ESDIS
- **Notes:** One day covers only ~10% of the US. Although Landsat 8 and 9 together revisit every 8 days, 8 days of GIBS images left about a third of the eastern US empty (checked for 30 Sep–7 Oct 2026). 16 days fill almost everything except a few small gaps. Clouds are not removed, and the edges between strips from different days are visible. The map shows the 16 days ending 4 days before the website was last published, refreshed monthly. The HLS_S30 layer (Sentinel-2, European) is not used because we focus on US sources.

## IMERG precipitation rate (latest)

- **Provider:** NASA GIBS (data: NASA GPM)
- **Link:** <https://nasa-gibs.github.io/gibs-api-docs/>
- **Access:** Tile service (WMTS), no login
- **Spatial resolution:** 0.1° (~10 km)
- **Temporal coverage:** Near real-time
- **Update frequency:** Every 30 minutes
- **Status:** Active
- **License / citation:** NASA open data. Acknowledge NASA GIBS / ESDIS

## GPM IMERG Final Precipitation L3 Monthly (GPM_3IMERGM v07)

- **Provider:** NASA GES DISC
- **Link:** <https://disc.gsfc.nasa.gov/datasets/GPM_3IMERGM_07/summary>
- **Access:** earthaccess (NASA Earthdata login)
- **Spatial resolution:** 0.1° (~10 km)
- **Temporal coverage:** 1998–present, monthly
- **Update frequency:** Monthly, ~3–4 months delay
- **Status:** Active
- **License / citation:** NASA open data. Cite: Huffman et al., GPM IMERG Final Precipitation L3 Monthly, V07, GES DISC

## Relative Oceanic Niño Index (RONI) v6

- **Provider:** NOAA Climate Prediction Center (CPC)
- **Link:** <https://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/products/analysis_monitoring/enso/roni/>
- **Access:** Plain text file download, no login
- **Spatial resolution:** Single index for the Niño 3.4 region (5°N–5°S, 120°–170°W)
- **Temporal coverage:** 1950–present, 3-month running seasons
- **Update frequency:** Monthly
- **Status:** Active
- **License / citation:** NOAA open data. Credit: NOAA Climate Prediction Center
- **Notes:** NOAA's main ENSO index since February 2026. It replaced the Oceanic Niño Index (ONI), which is still updated: https://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/products/analysis_monitoring/enso/oni/v6/. Calculated from ERSST v6. RONI v5 is also available. Recent values can change for up to two months after they are first posted.

## Multivariate ENSO Index Version 2 (MEI.v2)

- **Provider:** NOAA Physical Sciences Laboratory (PSL)
- **Link:** <https://psl.noaa.gov/enso/mei/>
- **Access:** Plain text file download, no login
- **Spatial resolution:** Single index for the tropical Pacific (30°S–30°N, 100°E–70°W)
- **Temporal coverage:** 1979–present, 2-month seasons (DJ, JF, …)
- **Update frequency:** Monthly
- **Status:** Active
- **License / citation:** NOAA open data. Credit NOAA PSL. Method: Wolter & Timlin (1993, 1998, 2011); Zhang et al. (2019)
- **Notes:** Combines five variables into one index without units: sea level pressure, sea surface temperature, east-west and north-south surface winds, and outgoing longwave radiation. Standardised against 1980–2018. Since March 2024 the whole series is calculated from the JRA-3Q reanalysis instead of JRA-55; the older values are kept in a separate file. NOAA also publishes a ready-made time series, lifecycle plot and correlation maps on the MEI page. The ±0.5 El Niño / La Niña lines on our chart are a widely used convention for MEI; NOAA's MEI page itself only says positive values mean El Niño and negative values La Niña.

## Climate Indices: Monthly Atmospheric and Ocean Time Series

- **Provider:** NOAA Physical Sciences Laboratory (PSL)
- **Link:** <https://psl.noaa.gov/data/climateindices/list/>
- **Access:** Plain text file download per index, no login
- **Spatial resolution:** Single indices; the region differs per index
- **Temporal coverage:** 1948 (some earlier)–present, monthly
- **Update frequency:** Monthly for indices marked * on the list; others irregularly or not at all
- **Status:** Active
- **License / citation:** NOAA open data. Credit NOAA PSL and the original provider of each index (e.g. NOAA CPC)
- **Notes:** About 40 monthly index series in one simple text format, one file per index: ENSO (Niño 1+2, 3, 3.4 and 4 sea surface temperature anomalies, ONI, MEI v2, SOI, BEST, TNI), NAO, PDO, AO, Atlantic SST and some regional rainfall. Only the indices marked * on the list are updated regularly; the four Niño regions and the SOI are among them. The map on the El Niño tab uses the four Niño regions.

## Optimum Interpolation Sea Surface Temperature (OISST) v2.1

- **Provider:** NOAA NCEI (served by NOAA CoastWatch ERDDAP)
- **Link:** <https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/products/optimum-interpolation-sst>
- **Access:** NetCDF from NOAA CoastWatch's ERDDAP server, no login. ERDDAP cuts out only the days and grid points we need
- **Spatial resolution:** 0.25° (~28 km); shown at 1° on the map
- **Temporal coverage:** 1981–present, daily
- **Update frequency:** Daily; the final version we use is about 2 weeks behind
- **Status:** Active
- **License / citation:** NOAA open data. Cite Huang et al. (2021), J. Climate. Served by NOAA CoastWatch ERDDAP
- **Notes:** Blends satellite, ship, buoy and Argo float data. Uses NCEI's daily anomalies, which are calculated against the 1971–2000 average. The map plays the last 52 weeks (Sunday to Saturday), each the average of its 7 daily anomalies. NOAA CPC's El Niño monitoring (and so RONI) uses the 1991–2020 average instead. The oceans have warmed since the 1970s, so these values run warmer than CPC's. NOAA uses OISST for maps of current conditions and ERSST (behind RONI) for comparing events across years. We first used NOAA PSL's copy of the same data, but since November 2026 PSL's data server (THREDDS) answers every request with "Too Many Requests", so we switched to ERDDAP. NCEI also has a preliminary version, closer to real time, that may still be revised.

## USGS daily streamflow (daily mean discharge) at stream gauges

- **Provider:** U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) Water Data for the Nation
- **Link:** <https://waterdata.usgs.gov/>
- **Access:** USGS Water Data API (api.waterdata.usgs.gov/ogcapi/v1), no login. Optional free API key
- **Spatial resolution:** Individual stream gauges, any US state (e.g. ~250 active in Washington)
- **Temporal coverage:** Varies by gauge, some since the late 1800s; daily
- **Update frequency:** Daily, values for yesterday usually available today
- **Status:** Active
- **License / citation:** USGS public domain. Cite: U.S. Geological Survey, National Water Information System, https://doi.org/10.5066/F7P55KJN
- **Notes:** Recent values are provisional and can be revised. Not every gauge measures streamflow every day. USGS is retiring its old WaterServices API (waterservices.usgs.gov): service degrades from November 2026 and it is switched off on 22 February 2027. We use the new Water Data API that replaces it.

## NOAA 7-Day Precipitation Departure from Normal

- **Provider:** NOAA National Weather Service / PRISM Climate Group
- **Link:** <https://mapservices.weather.noaa.gov/raster/services/obs/rfc_qpe/MapServer/WMSServer>
- **Access:** Public WMS service
- **Spatial resolution:** ~4 km
- **Temporal coverage:** Last 7 days (updated daily)
- **Update frequency:** Daily
- **Status:** Active
- **License / citation:** Public Domain. Normal values calculated by PRISM Climate Group (Oregon State University 30-year average).
